items.summary: Samsung Electronics reported operating profit of 107.4 trillion won for the July-to-October quarter, in line with its estimate and up from 12.2 trillion won a year earlier, driven by strong demand for AI chips. Shares rose as SK Hynix's upbeat outlook eased concerns about fading AI earnings momentum.
items.title: Samsung Posts Record Q3 Profit on AI Chip Demand

items.summary: Google parent Alphabet fell more than 10% in extended trading after missing profit and revenue expectations on Oct 28. Its third-quarter free cash flow was negative US$9.07 billion, up from US$5.9 billion a quarter earlier. Total revenue reached US$127.6 billion against an estimate of US$128.2 billion, while adjusted earnings per share of US$2.67 missed the Wall Street target of US$3.02. CFO Anat Ashkenazi said AI-driven capital expenditures would increase significantly in 2027 and that near-term margin pressure was expected from third-party cloud capacity use.
items.title: Alphabet Shares Drop After Revenue Miss and Rising AI Cash Burn

items.summary: Microsoft reported $10 billion in revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, including revenue-sharing payments and Azure services, for the quarter ended September 30, per a regulatory filing. That figure represents nearly 11% of Microsoft's total quarterly revenue of $92.3 billion. For fiscal year 2026, OpenAI-related revenue reached $24.1 billion.
items.title: Microsoft Reports $10 Billion in OpenAI Revenue for Quarter

items.summary: Microsoft reported a record quarter with revenue of $92.3 billion, up 19% over the year-ago period, marking its tenth consecutive quarterly record. Net income on a GAAP basis reached $36.6 billion, up 32%. Cloud drove growth to $63.9 billion, led by Azure at $33.2 billion and OpenAI revenue of $10 billion. Microsoft also noted capital expenditures topped $45.2 billion, another record.
items.title: Microsoft Posts Tenth Straight Quarter of Record Revenue

items.summary: Procore, a global construction management software provider serving tens of thousands of customers across the U.S., Europe, Middle East, Asia, and Australia, has built Procore Analytics 2.0 on a medallion architecture inside Databricks using OpenSharing to deliver governed data extracts into customer tools like Power BI, Tableau, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, and SQL Server. The upgrade replaced the older API-based system that capped refreshes at three times daily. Procore reports Analytics 2.0 expanded its table catalog from several years of work in version 1.0 to hundreds of tables in under half the time, effectively doubling extractable data surface area. Matthew Guptill, Product Manager for Procore Analytics, said OpenSharing has increased visibility across construction teams and helped deliver projects on time, budget, and safely.
items.title: Procore Builds OpenSharing Data Platform for Construction Analytics

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Anthropic has made three beta features generally available for Claude Enterprise plans: smart reports, pooled budgets, and in-app surveys. These tools track task usage, costs, friction points, and workflow opportunities while setting monthly spend caps per group and seat. The move comes as Anthropic faces scrutiny ahead of its IPO amid concerns about enterprise AI spending.
items.title: Anthropic Rolls Out AI ROI Tracking Tools for Enterprise Clients

items.summary: Amazon announced the new Echo Show 16, a 16-inch smart display with integrated Fire TV. The standard model starts at $500; the Nanomatte version costs $570. Amazon said its wide-angle camera doubles Visual ID range to 17 feet and the device has 20% more computing power than the Echo Show 15, which it claims is nearly 40% thinner with twice as vibrant colors.
items.title: Amazon debuts Echo Show 16, a large smart display with Fire TV

items.summary: Google DeepMind released Genie 4 as a research preview for trusted testers, describing it as its first real-time world model to generate audio natively alongside visuals. The system builds explorable worlds from text and image prompts in real time; users steer events with plain-language input while Gemini models act inside the simulation loop as planner, verifying frames and revising plans between inputs. DeepMind states the preview ran internal safety evaluations before release and will carry SynthID watermarks, starting today for trusted testers then expanding to Google AI Ultra subscribers and early-access partners. It discloses no parameters, resolution, frame rate or benchmarks; scene consistency holds up to 2 minutes, though sessions last only a few minutes and objects drift after repeated prompt edits.
items.title: Google DeepMind releases Genie 4 real-time world model with native audio

items.summary: Quoting Ted Sanders, a short piece argues that large language model performance is largely explained by one variable: model size, with bigger models being more performant but costlier. It then explains how OpenAI orders its own releases—Luna < Terra < Sol < Astra—and what version numbers like 6.1 convey about release order and improvement magnitude relative to prior versions such as 5.6 and the significance of a major jump to 7.
items.title: Ted Sanders Explains OpenAI's Model Naming Conventions

items.summary: BYD now employs more than 1.02 million people, according to chairman Wang Chuanfu, who shared the figures at the China Society of Automotive Engineers' 33rd annual conference on Wednesday. The headcount exceeds the combined workforce of Toyota, GM, Ford and Tesla by roughly 170,000. BYD reached this level after a hiring surge in late 2025 following an earlier cut to about 869,600 employees at year-end 2025. The article notes that most workers are based in China while sales grow overseas, and cautions that the large headcount reflects vertical integration rather than output alone: BYD produces roughly 5.3 vehicles per worker versus around 12 to 29 for its rivals.
items.title: BYD Surpasses Toyota, GM, Ford and Tesla in Total Workforce

items.summary: A Tesla owner writing seven years after paying $6,000 for a permanent Full Self-Driving subscription describes how the system has improved on his 2026 Model Y running FSD V14. He reports that it now handles trip start and end more often, reacts to edge cases such as school-zone lights slowing to 20 mph, speed bumps, crosswalks, deer, debris, and phantom braking, and can navigate garages and parking lots without intervention. He states he seldom must intervene or complain. The owner asserts in his own voice that FSD is a safety feature that has saved lives but criticizes Tesla for withholding it from customers who have not paid the $99/month fee, calling it choosing income over customer safety while noting Automatic Collision Evasion can work without engagement. He also asks whether limited Level 5 automation could be approved and offers referral links with promotional details about free Supercharging and discounts.
items.title: Tesla Owner Credits FSD for Fewer Interventions and Safety Gains

items.summary: European news sites report that the last new Polestar 2 has rolled off Luqiao assembly line in China, with more than 200,000 of the all-electric sedan/hatchbacks built since its 2020 launch. The company has not confirmed this officially, but it aligns with plans for an updated Polestar 2 in 2027 and a new Polestar 7 SUV by early 2028. Production ends as Polestar exits the US after the Trump Administration's Commerce Department declined authorization under the Connected Vehicle Rule earlier this year. The article then turns to EV deals, noting discounts on the Polestar 3 and 4 in the US market before promoting a solar installer service. (59 words)
items.title: Polestar Ends Polestar 2 Production After China Plant Closes

items.summary: Middle East nations renewed diplomatic efforts, with delegations from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan meeting Iranian officials in Tehran to explore a regional security framework. Standard Chartered expects an agreement could quickly reduce the geopolitical risk premium on oil, though prices will stay high until shipping lanes are secure and Gulf supply is reliable again. The U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve holds just 282.7 million barrels, its lowest level since 1982, per EIA figures. Standard Chartered says crude prices remain elevated over the coming months as disrupted production and costly shipping limit effective supply. On natural gas, TTF traded at €98.58/MWh on Wednesday amid seasonal tightening.
items.title: Oil Buyers Face $100-Plus Prices Despite Middle East Peace Talks

items.summary: European refineries closed a decade ago while Gulf states built new capacity, but recent Middle East conflict has damaged key facilities in Saudi Arabia and Russia. IEA chief Fatih Birol warns crude and gas prices stay elevated next year as refined-product supply cannot be rerouted like raw oil. Ukraine's drone strikes hit 30 Russian refineries—80% of national capacity, down from 6.1 million to an estimated 1.6 million barrels daily. A Trump–Putin deal sends only 300,000 tons (75,000 barrels a day) of diesel abroad, which analysts call negligible against global demand. Russia raised refining output ~25% in October to about 5 million barrels daily via local repairs, yet the shortage persists and further attacks loom after planned U.S. midterm hostilities with Iran on November 3.
items.title: Refinery Damage Deepens Global Fuel Shortage

items.summary: Samsung Electronics reported operating profit of 107.4 trillion won ($80.04 billion) for the July-to-September quarter, nearly nine times the year earlier figure of 12.2 trillion won, matching its own estimate. The gain reflects strong AI chip demand, though investors remain cautious about whether spending will hold.
items.title: Samsung Posts Record Q3 Profit on AI Chip Demand

items.summary:
Microsoft reported total revenue of $92.3bn in the September quarter, above analysts' expectation of around $90.6bn, with more than $36.6bn in profit versus an expected $35.1bn, per a securities filing cited by the company and FactSet figures respectively. Growth was driven largely by Azure cloud computing, which rose 48%. The report followed voluntary buyouts offered to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as it increases AI spending. Chief executive Satya Nadella said the business delivers greater capability, choice, control and cost-efficiency for customers across its stack.

visual null},
items.title: Microsoft beats revenue and profit forecasts amid staff buyouts

items.summary: Apple claims its new M6-powered MacBook Pro delivers up to 13 times faster first-token performance for LLM prompts than the older M1 model, and promises up to 16 hours of wireless web browsing. The 14-inch OLED display reaches 1,600 nits with a 120Hz refresh rate. Launched in India on October 27, it starts at ₹2,39,900, with upgrades pushing the final price higher. Pre-orders are open and Indian sales begin November 6.
items.title: Apple's OLED MacBook Pro 2026 carries a costly price catch

items.summary: Google parent Alphabet reported disappointing third-quarter results, sending its shares down about 10 per cent after hours. Total revenue of $127.6 billion missed estimates, driven by a $1.4-billion shortfall in advertising that offset gains from Google Cloud revenues more than doubling to $30.71 billion. The company posted negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion and burned $5.9 billion last quarter, the first loss in 22 years as a public company. CFO Anat Ashkenazi said she expected near-term margin pressure from third-party cloud capacity. Investors also worried about higher 2027 capital spending forecasts of $205 billion versus this year's $195 billion. Analysts questioned whether Google rushed AI model deployment amid softer financial metrics.
items.title: Alphabet shares fall as search miss and AI cash burn weigh on results

items.summary: In Tokyo, Ryua moved into a rental apartment after seeing a man glare at her during a viewing; since the agent could not see him, she concluded he was a ghost and chose to stay. She reports daily paranormal activity four years later. The property carries a roughly 30% rent discount on its small bedsit in Setagaya. Diane Tincher, an American living in rural Kagoshima for nearly 40 years, bought a three-bedroom house for about half the usual price after an elderly woman died alone there. She researched it via Oshimaland, a crowdsourced site listing stigmatised properties launched in 2005 and expanded internationally by 2011. Founder Teru Oshima notes such homes were once unattractive options; a 2025 survey found more than half of Japanese people would now rent one if cheap.
items.title: Japan's haunted homes draw bargain hunters amid rising prices

items.summary: KPMG's 2026 India CEO Outlook reports that 87% of Indian chief executive officers are confident about their organisations' growth prospects over the next three years, up from 83% in 2025. Confidence in India's broader growth stands at 73%, compared with 71% a year earlier. The survey raises questions about whether this optimism will translate into faster investment, stronger earnings and sustained hiring amid geopolitical tensions, economic uncertainty and technological disruption.
items.title: Indian CEOs Expect Growth Despite Uncertainty, KPMG Survey Finds

items.summary: The article examines John Healey’s budget, in which nearly every consumer-facing measure returned to the cost of energy as inflation rose and GDP growth was cut from 1.6% to 1%. The £100 payment to 20m households in A-D council tax bands is described as its sole surprise, funded partly by a bank surcharge lasting 15 months. EDF predicts the regulator’s price cap will rise by £466 in January, pushing an average household bill to £2,189, up from £1,568 when Labour took office in July 2024. Healey signals “deep reform of our energy system,” but the author argues the plan is still blurry and lacks urgency, with electrification policies underpowered and market reforms unfinished.
items.title: Labour’s energy policy remains half-formed amid rising bills

items.summary: Prediction market Kalshi hired political strategist Eric Schultz as an out-of-house adviser, a person familiar with the matter told Semafor. The hiring arrives amid Democratic forecasts in Tuesday’s midterms: Kalshi users put odds at 91% for a House majority and 65% for a Senate majority. Kalshi declined to comment.
items.title: Kalshi hires Obama adviser Eric Schultz

items.summary: Brazil's main stock index fell further on Wednesday as fears over the country's fiscal outlook grew after Flávio Bolsonaro lost a surprise election and fled to the US. Finance minister Paulo Guedes said the selloff reflected unwinding of pre-election bets rather than fundamentals, with some analysts calling it an opportunity. A Bloomberg columnist linked the volatility to prediction markets that briefly generated around $130 billion in stock market wealth before it vanished.
items.title: Investors Watch Brazilian Stocks After Election-Driven Selloff

items.summary: Senate estimates revealed the Department of Employment and Workplace Relations received just 50 applications for compensation over its Centrelink cancellation error, having sent only 1,430 invitations. The department said it would proactively contact about 50,000 people affected by an operation that unlawfully cut income from an estimated 310,000 people between 2020 and 2024.
items.title: Centrelink compensation applications far outnumber invitations sent amid TCF bungle fallout

items.summary: In Gaza and the West Bank, many Palestinians focus less on Israel's election result than on whether it would bring real change. Whether Benjamin Netanyahu stays in power with his far-right allies or centrist rival Gadi Eisenkot wins, few expect hope from Tuesday's vote. Huda al-Houli, a displaced resident of Khan Younis, said they fear the elections could bring an even worse leader.
items.title: Palestinians See Little Hope in Israeli Election Outcome

items.summary: The New South Wales parliament passed legislation creating the Great Koala National Park, which campaigners called a historic win after more than a decade of campaigning. The park will span 475,000 hectares (1.2 million acres), incorporating 178,000 hectares (440,000 acres) of state forests and other government land into the national estate before opening by end of 2026. Long-term funding relies on Australian Carbon Credit Units under the Improved Native Forest Management method, an approach critics say risks greenwashing conservation. Multiple attempts to amend the scheme were voted down in parliament.
items.title: NSW Approves Great Koala National Park on Carbon-Funded Terms

items.summary: Japan and the US agreed Wednesday (Oct 28) to set up a Japanese facility for jointly producing advanced medium-range air-to-air missiles used by F-35 fighter jets, according to Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi. The announcement came during his meeting with US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in Cebu, Philippines. Koizumi called the project part of “Operation Supercharge” and said the missiles are essential for the F-35 but gave no further details.
items.title: US and Japan Agree on Missile Production Facility in Cebu

items.summary: Canada and the European Union agreed in a joint declaration to pursue closer ties but dropped a proposal for associate EU membership ahead of a Montreal summit. Prime Minister Mark Carney aims to reduce Canada's reliance on the US amid Trump tariffs, though critics warn the move risks angering Washington.
items.title: Canada and EU Drop Associate Membership Plan Amid Trade Tensions

items.summary: Muamer Nukic, a 51-year-old Protective Services Group employee with Queensland Police, pleaded guilty to making nine offensive and antisemitic comments on Threads. The court found that in the post he advocated for violence and rape. He was sentenced to a nine-month good-behaviour bond and fined $1,000.
items.title: Queensland Police Employee Fined Over Antisemitic Social Media Comments

items.summary: Craig Winder, director of Victoria Crime News and a home security business, admitted his credited local reporters do not exist; workers in the Philippines write stories attributed to fictitious Australian journalists. ABC NEWS Verify reported VCN has filed over 250 articles since February 2026 while crediting a four-person team, and that AI chatbots recommend it as reliable despite glaring errors and AI-generated images. Momoko Fujita of the University of Canberra called it 'pink slime' journalism. Winder said he set up the site to raise awareness of crime in his state and compel government action, but conceded using fake bios was somewhat deceptive.
items.title: Victoria crime news site owner admits using Filipino writers

items.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro, a defeated presidential candidate, and his family arrived in the U.S. after Brazilian authorities ordered him to surrender his passport. He faces multiple investigations in Brazil.
items.title: Defeated Flavio Bolsonaro Arrives in Miami Amid Brazilian Investigations

items.summary: A high-speed train collision killed at least 68 people and injured dozens more on Wednesday morning around 140km south of Madrid, between Mora and Orgaz. The Renfe-operated train was struck from behind by an Iryo train that had stopped for a computer failure; several carriages fell down an embankment. Transport Minister Óscar Puente said the crash followed a system failure and human error in Madrid's control centre, calling it one of Europe's worst disasters and Spain's deadliest since 2013. Survivors described passengers thrown into the air, fire and dead bodies. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called for an investigation amid national grief.
items.title: Spain's deadliest train crash in over a decade kills at least 68

items.summary: Two high-speed passenger trains travelling from Madrid to Seville collided in Spain, the item reports. A computer failure in the automatic signalling system had halted all trains on a stretch of line. Passengers say one train was then ordered to proceed and crashed into the rear of the other between Mora and Orgaz, about 140km (87 miles) south of Madrid. Survivors described carriages destroyed, debris everywhere and people thrown from their seats; some were trapped or injured. Spain's transport minister Óscar Puente called it 'truly unbelievable'. The accident has raised questions for authorities amid the country's recent rail safety concerns after 46 deaths in January at Adamuz near Córdoba. Affected passengers expressed anger that no warning had been given to the driver of the second train.
items.title: Spanish rail collision after trains wrongly cleared to proceed

items.summary: The Netherlands pledged $500 million over 10 years to the Tropical Forest Forever Facility (TFFF), a long-term conservation fund launched by Brazil at COP30 in November 2025. Its creator estimates the TFFF could protect 800 to 900 million hectares of tropical forest, roughly 200 times the size of the Netherlands. Environmental economist Bard Harstad criticized concerns about its economic solvency and political reversibility, while conservationist Merijn van Leeuwen called it a major breakthrough for global forest protection.
items.title: Netherlands Pledges $500 Million to Tropical Forest Forever Facility

items.summary: Rescuers worked overnight near Urda, using cranes to lift wreckage from mangled carriages at the site of a collision between two high-speed trains. The disaster killed at least 68 people and injured more than 100 on 28 October, making it Spain's second deadly rail collision this year. In Madrid, dozens held a minute of silence in Cibeles Square; opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo attended as the gathering turned into a protest calling for Transport Minister Óscar Puente to resign.
items.title: Madrid mourns and protests after deadly Spanish train crash

items.summary: Rescue teams worked overnight near Urda, using cranes to lift wreckage from two high-speed trains that collided on 28 October. The accident is Spain's second deadly rail collision this year and one of Europe's deadliest railway accidents of the century. In Madrid, dozens gathered in Cibeles Square for a minute of silence organised by the Spanish Federation of Municipalities and Provinces, attended by opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo and Mayor José Luis Martínez-Almeida. The gathering turned into a protest against Transport Minister Óscar Puente, with participants holding placards reading 'Corruption kills' and chanting for his resignation.
items.title: Madrid mourns train crash victims as rescuers work through the night

items.summary: Vitalii Kim, Ukraine's Minister for Veterans Affairs, told FRANCE 24 that Ukraine will fight regardless of European support. Speaking in Paris amid uncertainty over a €90 billion aid package and speculation about Trump-mediated talks, he said "we also will fight because it's our motherland." He acknowledged public exhaustion from relentless bombardment and strikes on energy infrastructure, while outlining plans to reintegrate an estimated 1.5 million veterans with expanded mental healthcare.
items.title: Ukraine's Minister Vows to Fight Despite EU Aid Uncertainty

items.summary: Treasury bill cutoff yields rose about 20 basis points above the previous auction, reaching their highest level in nearly two years. Traders attributed this to near deficit liquidity and elevated crude prices driving a higher liquidity premium. The 91-day yield came in at 5.93%, while longer tenures reached 6.54% for 182 days and 6.69% for 364 days, per RBI data.
items.title: RBI Treasury Bill Yields Reach Two-Year High Amid Liquidity Tightening and Oil Prices

items.summary: Google parent Alphabet missed profit and revenue expectations as accelerated AI spending widened its cash burn, sending shares down more than 10% in extended trading. Free cash flow fell to $9.07 billion versus near breakeven estimates, while total revenue reached $127.6 billion against a $128.2 billion estimate. CFO Anat Ashkenazi said capex would rise significantly in 2027 and warned of margin pressure from third-party cloud capacity.
items.title: Alphabet Shares Fall After AI Spending Drives Earnings Miss

items.summary: Billionaire Gautam Adani is exploring a potential acquisition of Dutch energy storage group VTTI, people familiar with the matter said. A deal could value the company at around €3 billion ($3.4 billion), they said. Deliberations are ongoing and there’s no certainty they’ll result in a transaction, the people said. Spokespeople for IFM, Adnoc and VTTI declined to comment; an Adani Group representative didn’t immediately respond.
items.title: Adani Explores €3 Billion VTTI Energy Storage Deal

items.summary: On its debut listing, Jio Platforms became the second most valued company in India and fifth most valued telecom services provider globally. It listed at Rs 1,358, a 21% premium over its Rs 1,119 IPO price, closing at Rs 1,419, up 27%. The listing gave it a market capitalisation of Rs 13.1 lakh crore, behind only Reliance Industries (Rs 15.7 lakh crore) but ahead of Bharti Airtel (Rs 12.2 lakh crore). Jio has about 54 crore customers.
items.title: Jio Platforms debuts as India’s second most valuable company

items.summary: Microsoft shares rose more than five percent Wednesday after the company reported total revenue of $92.3 billion and profit of more than $36.6 billion, figures it attributed to its Azure cloud division growing 48 percent in the September quarter. Analysts had expected around $90.6 billion in revenue and $35.1 billion in profit, according to FactSet.
items.title: Microsoft Shares Rise on Strong Azure Growth and Quarterly Earnings

items.summary: Several mutual fund houses have temporarily halted fresh investments in Gold Funds of Funds since mid-October, affecting lump-sum purchases, new SIP registrations and switch-ins. The Economic Times explains that investors can instead consider Gold ETFs, which remain open to new investment despite the FoF restrictions.
items.title: Gold FoFs Face Fresh Investment Restrictions Amid Market Uncertainty

items.summary: Wednesday, Jio Platforms listed on the National Stock Exchange as the 3,138th company following India's largest public offering. A listing pop of 21.36% made it the second most valuable Indian company by market cap, while parent Reliance Industries Group became the country's largest conglomerate, surpassing Tata Group. Patriarch Mukesh Ambani showed emotion as his children spoke at the bell-ringing ceremony attended by four generations.
items.title: Jio Platforms Lists on NSE as Ambani Family Celebrates Milestone

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi mocked the Congress party on X Wednesday, asking how many seats it won in Legislative Council elections across four states. The opposition secured none of the 28 ballot-paper seats.
items.title: Modi mocks Congress over MLC election rout

items.summary: The Supreme Court directed Shiv Sena (UBT) Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut to appear in person on Wednesday over a contempt petition for remarks against Chief Justice Surya Kant and the judiciary. A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi called the matter important as it concerns the entire institution of the judiciary. Journalist Nikhil Wagle, facing the same charge of scandalising the institution, was exempted from physical appearance and asked to appear virtually after being represented by a lawyer in court proceedings on Wednesday.
items.title: Supreme Court Summons Sanjay Raut in Contempt Case Over Judiciary Remarks

items.summary: At the Jio Platforms IPO listing ceremony in Mumbai, Reliance chairman Mukesh Ambani was visibly moved and wiped tears from his eyes while listening to speeches by his children Anant and Isha Ambani. The next-generation executives reflected on the company's growth, family vision, and societal reach of Jio.
items.title: Reliance Chairman Wipes Tears at Jio IPO Ceremony

items.summary: Persistent Systems could raise around Rs 6,000 crore through non-convertible debentures (NCDs) to fund its acquisition of Nagarro. The debt would replace an 18-month bridge loan from Barclays and match the company's cash flows over tenures up to five years with an average maturity of about three years. Persistent had earlier raised Rs 4,264 crore via a QIP.
items.title: Persistent Systems Plans Rs 6,000 Crore Debt Raise for Nagarro Acquisition

items.summary: Petrol and diesel prices stayed unchanged across several Indian cities on October 29, while CNG rose in many locations. Chennai, Mathura and Meerut saw ₹2 increases; Mumbai, Bengaluru and Sonipat added ₹1 each; Bharatpur, Dewas and Firozabad recorded rises of 50 paise. Hyderabad had the highest petrol price at ₹116.15, while Chandigarh was lowest at ₹101.54. Diesel ranged from ₹89.47 in Chandigarh to ₹104.40 in Thiruvananthapuram. CNG climbed across several cities but stayed unchanged in New Delhi, Hyderabad, Rewari and NCR. Prices were taken from Goodreturns by LiveMint's Sounak Mukhopadhyay.
items.title: Indian Fuel Prices Steady as CNG Rises in Many Cities

items.summary: A report merged Thursday claimed at least three documents among the released Jeffrey Epstein files indicate that classified information was included, though what exactly was classified remains unclear. CBC News reported one document shows the Office of the Deputy Attorney General received classified material related to Epstein in March 2025. The DOJ has maintained the files contain no national security secrets and says it collected about 6 million pages but released over 3 million after review. CBS News analysis found tens of thousands of missing pages, including around 1.2 million gaps in one sequence, suggesting documents were removed without clear reason.
items.title: Report flags gaps and classified clues in Epstein file release

items.summary: Finshots examined Swiggy's second-quarter FY27 results and questioned whether its quick-commerce arm, Instamart, is outpacing the food delivery business. Adjusted revenue rose 34% to ₹7,909 crore while adjusted EBITDA reached ₹341 crore. However, Instamart's adjusted loss widened to ₹895 crore as Swiggy added 69 net dark stores and spent on pricing initiatives like the ₹9 Store. The outlet noted that growth may not yet justify costs and compared Instamart against Blinkit, suggesting profitability depends on scale. Swiggy reported a closing cash balance of ₹13,662 crore to fund expansion.
items.title: Swiggy's Instamart Losses Widened as Quick Commerce Investment Grows

items.summary: India's Special Intensive Revision of voter rolls has drawn concern over the possible disenfranchisement of eligible voters and its resemblance to a citizenship test. The revision, begun in Bihar in June 2025, presumes eligibility only from two-decade-old rolls, so most people under about 40 must link through a parent or grandparent or produce documents. In 2025 the Association for Democratic Reforms challenged it in the Supreme Court; on May 27 the court allowed limited enquiry into citizenship but left how to conduct it unclear. By September 1, draft rolls were missing 13.37 crore names. Veena Naregal of the Institute of Economic Growth argues a method refined over welfare schemes has now reached every voter.
items.title: Supreme Court Clears Path for Citizenship Checks in Voter Roll Revision

items.summary: Former Sri Lanka captain Kumar Sangakkara alleged that Ryanair staff threatened and discriminated against his family at a Dublin airport, posting the account on X. Describing it as shocking and his first unpleasant experience in Ireland, he exchanged messages with Sanjiva Weerawarana about discrimination abroad. At writing, Ryanair had not responded to his claims.
items.title: Sangakkara Alleges Discrimination by Ryanair Staff in Dublin

items.summary:
The Supreme Court directed the Election Commission of India not to force nearly 4.3 million Delhi voters removed from electoral rolls during the special intensive revision (SIR) to reapply via Form 6, suggesting they instead use Form 8 or enumeration processes if on the 2026 roll. The bench urged officials to proactively reach out rather than burdening migrants who move frequently. It questioned whether algorithm-driven 'logical discrepancy' classifications involved meaningful human review and noted the category disenfranchised 2.71 million people in West Bengal, where it remains an interim arrangement only. The court set a two-week deadline for ECI to respond before rehearing the matter on October 30.

visual null
items.title: Supreme Court Questions Election Commission Over Voter Disenfranchisement Notices

items.summary: A fire gutted several shops at the Vasco Sunday Market in Goa late Wednesday night, starting near Tilak Maidan. Chief Minister Pramod Sawant visited the site with MLAs and assured government support for those affected. He said administrative staff were working to control the blaze while more details on its cause remain awaited.
items.title: Goa Chief Minister Assures Support After Vasco Sunday Market Fire Damages Shops

items.summary: Twenty-seven years after the 1999 Staines murders in Manoharpur, Odisha, a community lives in fear that convict Dara Singh's release could embolden extremist elements as attacks on churches intensify. The Odisha government told the Supreme Court on September 17 it opposes his release for now, citing concerns over communal tensions after about 200–250 Dara Sena members gathered outside Keonjhar jail on August 15, 2026. Witness Samson Marandi warned that harmony is 'certain to be under threat.' Church leader Jagat Ranjan Santra blamed the government's stance on political calculations and pointed to a surge in violence since the BJP came to power in 2024, including an incident where pastor Bipin Bihari Naik was assaulted. While Dara Sena member Ranjan Kumar Sahoo expressed confidence in Singh's release after 26 years, others remain divided over whether he has changed.
items.title: Odisha Christians Fear Dara Singh Release Amid Rising Church Attacks

items.summary: The Federal reports that Maldivian President Mohammed Muizzu's state visit to Pakistan, his first as head of state in over a decade, included two defence memoranda of understanding—one broad and one on maritime security—that the outlet frames as threats to New Delhi. During his three-day trip, Islamabad and Male signed 20 MoUs and set a bilateral trade target of $200 million from an existing $13 million. The article argues Malé's 'Maldives First' policy risks deepening a China-Pakistan nexus in the Indian Ocean archipelago and revives concerns over extremism. It concludes that India must sustain its engagement, though it notes New Delhi-Male ties have remained relatively stable.
items.title: Maldives' Pakistan defence MoUs alarm India over strategic shift

items.summary: An 18-year-old student preparing for competitive exams died by hanging herself at a hostel in Bhanwarkuan, Indore on Tuesday night. The room stayed locked until police found her dead; no suicide note was recovered. Her roommate had left for work, leaving her alone. Police will seize her mobile phone to investigate the circumstances.
items.title: Indore Aspirant Dies By Suicide At Hostel As Police Investigate

items.summary: A security guard from Mhow died after slipping and falling beneath a train while alighting at platform number two of Indore railway station on Tuesday night. Mohammad Israel, who worked for a private company in Indore, had travelled to the city for his night-shift duty. Survived by a son studying and a daughter whose marriage was fixed in Pune for two months away, he died just before the wedding preparations.
items.title: Mhow Security Guard Dies After Slipping From Train Before Daughter's Wedding
